You use needn't + have + past participle for actions which were performed but were unnecessary:

We needn't have bought any milk. We still have plenty at home.
(we bought some milk, but it wasn't necessary)
No one needs to travel two days or more just to receive a simple blood test.
Adverb clauses can explain the reason or purpose of an action. You use the conjunctions that, so that, in order that and lest to introduce the clause.
You use so that or just so in speaking rather than in order that.

We drink that we may live.
She works hard so that she will become successful.
Put on your warm coat lest you should catch a chill.
Shops were closed early in order that people might get home before the storm.
Shops were closed early so people might get home before the storm.

Lest means that…not, and, therefore, it will be wrong to add another not in the following clause. Moreover it should be noted that the only auxiliary verb that can be used after lest is should.
  • Reserve your seats early lest you miss the chance. OR Reserve your seats early lest you should miss the chance.(NOT Reserve your seats early lest you do not miss the chance.)

images.text: Hi everyone, thank you so much for coming to the first ever Bracelet of Hope charity auction! I'm so proud to be working for such a progressive undertaking, and I'm so grateful that you all could make it. For those of you who don't know me, my name is Amy Watson. I'm going to start by telling you a little about our philosophy. We believe poverty needn't be a death sentence. Instead, we believe that we need to focus on economic stabilization in order that improvements in health be realized. If you look around, you'll see images of children who live in our foster homes. They needn't have been orphaned. It is avoidable, and you can help.

With that in mind, let me tell you about one of our projects that needs funding. We hope to build medical centers so that patients can receive care in their home town. No one need travel two days or more just to receive a simple blood test. In many countries, the phrases “lest we forget” and “they died that we may live” have been adopted in remembrance of those fallen in battle. Here at Bracelet of Hope, we recite these mottos so that we don't forget the orphans for whom we are working. We recite them lest these children be forgotten.

Some of you might be thinking that I needn't be so dramatic, but there is really no other way of conveying the gravity of this crisis. Please bid and donate generously today, and do so with the knowledge that your funds will be used to alleviate the suffering of these brave children. Thank you.
